This dashboard provides a comprehensive overview of **Microsoft Active Directory (AD)** health and performance, designed to help you monitor domain controllers, replication, and authentication activity in real time.

It visualizes key performance counters collected from **Windows Server’s NTDS, Netlogon, Security System-Wide Statistics, DFS Replication,** and **DHCP** services. By tracking these metrics, you can quickly detect replication bottlenecks, authentication latency, service degradation, and capacity constraints before they impact users or applications.

Enable the Active Directory integration in your Datadog account to easily search, filter, and alert on all of these critical events in Datadog.

For configuration instructions, see:
[Active Directory Integration Documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/active_directory/)

To enable service checks, see the [Service checks](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/active-directory/#service-checks) section of the Active Directory docs.
For service states, see [Windows Service check states](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/windows-service/#service-checks):
- `OK`: Green
- `CRITICAL`: Red
- `UNKNOWN`: Gray
- `WARNING`: Yellow

definition.content:
The Kafka Broker metrics here inform you of data loss/delay through unclean leader elections, network throughputs, and request fails through request purgatories and timeouts metrics.

To access these metrics you need to have the [Kafka Broker](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/kafka/?tab=host) integration enabled.

Kafka Producers send messages to brokers for storage and distribution by topic. These metrics inform you of the volume and rate of data sent, and the success rate of message delivery.

To access these metrics you need to have the [Kafka Broker](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/kafka/?tab=host) integration enabled.

Kafka Consumer metrics provide insights into lag between message production and consumption, success rates and latency of message delivery, and the volume of data consumed.

To access these metrics you need to have the [Kafka Broker](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/kafka/?tab=host) and [Kafka Consumer](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/kafka-consumer/?tab=host) integrations enabled.

Get insights into your topics' producers and consumers, including anomaly detection by instrumenting with Data Streams Monitoring. 
Open in [Data Streams Monitoring](/data-streams) or [Learn More](https://docs.datadoghq.com/data_streams/setup/technologies/kafka/?referrer=kafka).

Assign the **topic** variable to view insights about a specific topic

definition.content: Zookeeper is a distributed coordination service for Kafka clusters. It coordinates activities like leader election, partition reassignment, and broker registration. This group will only be populated if you are using Zookeeper and have enabled [Datadog's Zookeeper Integration](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/zk/?tab=host). Running Zookeeper is not mandatory if you are using Kafka version 3.0 onwards, in which case, you can delete this group.

Kafka brokers are Java applications that expose JVM metrics to inform on the broker's system health. Garbage collection metrics like those below provide key insights into free memory, broker performance, and heap size. You need to enable [new_gc_metrics](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/java/?tab=host#configuration-options) for this section to populate.

When investigating logs, you can refer to the timeseries data to see the ratio of a certain log status to other expected statuses. In situations where you notice an increase in the ratio of error logs, you can refer to the log stream set up to filter erroneous logs for your perusal.

definition.content: Latency measures the **time between a client request and the server response**, and monitoring it enables you to detect changes in Redis performance. The single-threaded nature of Redis means that a long response time for one request increases the latency for all subsequent requests, leading to serious bottlenecks.

Memory usage is a crucial performance factor. If `used_memory > total available system memory`, the OS will begin swapping old/unused sections of memory and writing them to disk. Writing or reading from disk is up to 100,000 times slower than writing or reading from memory (0.1 µs for memory vs. 10 ms for disk).

formulas.alias: Keys evicted due to the maxmemory limit

definition.content: Redis has 10,000 client connections available by default, but you can adjust the maximum number of connections with the `maxclient` directive in redis.conf. New connection attempts will be refused if your Redis instance is currently at its maximum number of connections.
